Commentary.Commentary: That is it from this game and the action now switches to Visakhapatnam for the second ODI of the series. It will be a very important encounter as India will look to seal the series whereas Australia will look to get back on level terms and make the 3rd and final game all the more interesting. The 2nd ODI will be played on Sunday, the 19th of March and will begin at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT). You can though join us for the build-up a lot earlier. Cheers!

Ravindra Jadeja is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his brilliant all-round display. He says that he is playing ODI cricket after 8 months and was just trying to adapt to the format. Adds that he was looking to build a partnership with KL Rahul and even though the target wasn't a big one, it was necessary. Mentions that you need to alter your length and pace as it is different from Test cricket and he told himself to just hit the right spots and let the ball do the job. Says that he and Rahul tried to put on 70-80 runs and that is what happened and it wasn't easy to play the big shots on this wicket.

Hardik Pandya, the captain of India says that it was a good win. Adds that they were under pressure in both innings, but kept their composure and found ways to come out of those situations. Tells that when they got the momentum, they did not let that go. Praises Ravindra Jadeja for the way he played after coming back in ODIs after a long time. Says that he enjoyed his bowling and batting, but would have loved to stay there till the end. Ends by saying that it was great to see KL Rahul and Jadeja from the outside and that he is proud of the team.

Australian skipper, Steven Smith says that they weren't expecting this at the Wankhede and credits India for the way they bowled, and says that they should have got to a score of around 250. He then also commends KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja for the way they batted. Mentions that Mitchell Marsh played really well but they lost a lot of wickets in the middle and even after a strong bowling effort, India were always one good partnership away from victory. Reckons that they should have got 260-270 runs as the wicket wasn't that good and ball swung for almost 30 overs for both teams.
The Presentation ceremony...

The man of the moment, KL Rahul is down for a quick chat. Rahul says that losing three wickets early and with Mitchell Starc moving the ball around he wanted to play out the first 20-25 balls without thinking much about runs as the total was not that big. Adds that a couple of boundaries early on took the pressure off him. Tells that whoever he batted with, the plan was not to go into a shell and play their game. Mentions that he enjoyed batting with Hardik Pandya and Ravindra Jadeja and they wanted to run hard and put the loose balls away. Says that when the left-hander walked in, he got a few loose balls too and praises Ravindra Jadeja for the way he batted. Further adds that he did not think that the pitch would help the bowlers that much and credits Mohammad Shami for his brilliant spell. Ends by saying that he enjoyed his keeping and says when there is bounce, he loves it, but if it keeps low it turns out to be a challenge physically.

Earlier in the game, Hardik Pandya won the toss and put Australia into bat. This turned out to be a fine decision as Mohammed Siraj got rid of Travis Head early on. After that though, Mitchell Marsh counter-attacked and made everyone believe that it was a typical Wankhede wicket. At the other end, batters got starts but got out and the moment Marsh fell for a blistering 81, the Indian bowlers simply made short work of the tall Aussie batting order. The likes of Cameron Green, Glenn Maxwell and Marcus Stoinis couldn't contribute much and the spinners along with Mohammad Shami ripped through them. Siraj then came on to knocked over the tail and joined Shami on three wickets for the game. With a mediocre score on the board, it was a big effort from the Australian quicks early on in the chase to make a real match out of it but in the end, KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja took India to victory with a calm head.

Australia will feel a tad disappointed in the end but it was really their batting that let them down. Mitchell Starc looked like a man on a mission when the Aussies came out to bowl and got the ball to talk in the air and off the deck as well. Soon, he picked up three wickets and all the other bowlers kept things really tight as well to build on pressure. Their spinners though were largely ineffective and once the ball got old and there was a bit of dew, conditions eased out for batting and the Aussies didn't have much of an answer after that, succumbing to a defeat.

India were absolutely reeling at 16/3 and then at 39/4 but KL Rahul was holding one end when skipper Hardik Pandya walked out to bat. The pair steadied the ship a bit and just when things looked to get easier for them, Pandya too fell with 106 runs still needed for victory. Rahul showed brilliant composure and Ravindra Jadeja supported him valiantly. The pair dug deep to get through a lot of deliveries but once the margin of victory was under 50 runs, they started to bat freely as well. Rahul ended with an unbeaten 75 with Jadeja notching up 45 important runs as well.

Well, no one saw that coming! The Wankhede stadium is generally known for high-octane and high-scoring clashes but this game was all about digging in deep and in the end, India managed to get over the line, thanks to a gritty unbeaten stand between KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja worth 108 runs. The hosts have a 1-0 lead in the three-game ODI series and will now look to seal the series in the next game itself.

Drinks! India need 77 runs now and it looks like the upper hand is with them with both KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja batting sensibly. They will hope to finish this without losing any more wickets. Australia, on the other hand knows that one wicket here could change the momentum again and they are trying hard to get that. A good battle is going on between theses two sides and we can expect some more exciting cricket.

OUT! TAKEN! Marcus Stoinis strikes! The short ball plan has worked for Australia and Hardik Pandya has to walk back now. Stoinis bangs in a bouncer, on middle and leg, Hardik Pandya is not expecting it, but goes with his instincts and tries for the pull shot. However, he gets hurried and mistimes it as the ball travels in the air towards deep square leg where Cameron Green runs to his right and pouches it safely. India lose half their side now!
Commentary.Howout: c Cameron Green b Marcus Stoinis

Good length outside off and swinging away, KL Rahul looks to play at it but pulls out of the shot.

Beaten! Pitches this one up and pushes it well wide of the off stump, swinging it away. KL Rahul is drawn into the cover drive and he ends up reaching for it a bit. Rahul is beaten past the outside edge.
A touch fuller on off, skidding through, Gill looks to drive off the front foot but mistimes it toward wide mid on for a single.
Length again, angling into the stumps from around off, Gill solidly keeps it out.
Leg bye! A length ball, swinging into the pads, KL Rahul misses the flick and the ball goes off the pads behind square on the leg side. The batters pick up a leg bye.
Full on middle and leg, driven firmly but straight to mid on.

EDGED AND FOUR! A scrambled seam delivery, pitched up around off and angling across, Shubman Gill pushes at it and gets an outside edge, well wide of the second slip and runs away into the third man fence for a boundary.
Length ball outside off at 143.7 clicks, curving back in nicely. Shubman Gill punches it sweetly on the up but straight to extra cover.
WIDE! Good length, slanted well across the right-hander, Shubman Gill tries to reach it but can't get there. A wide is called.
Pitched up on the fourth stump line and going straight on. Shubman Gill watchfully leaves it alone.
Bowls it full and wide now, looking for the big inswinger but the ball goes straight on. Shubman Gill doesn't play at it.
Length ball at 142.5 clicks and right on the money, Shubman Gill solidly blocks it out.
PEACH! Immaculate length, in that channel around off and straightening off the deck. KL Rahul looks to block but the ball just zips past the outside edge.
Good length around middle and angling in, Rahul pushes it out toward mid on.
Pitches it up a bit around off, KL Rahul leans forward and plays at it late with soft hands. Ends up edging it well in front of the man at second slip.
Good length around off, kept out by Rahul.
On a hard length around off, Gill hangs back and taps it through point for a run.
Pitched up around off, seaming in late off the deck, Gill makes an assured leave.
Halt! KL Rahul is feeling a bit of stiffness on his neck. The physio is in to check on him. We are good to continue now.
Back of a length around off, Gill punches it nicely off the back foot toward cover and gets across for a single.
Shorter one around the body, Rahul dabs it toward mid-wicket for a single.
Nicely bowled! Good length, close to the off stump and angling across. KL Rahul plays inside the line of the ball.
On a good length over middle, KL Rahul allows the ball to swing and blocks it late onto the deck.
WIDE! A length ball on the pads, swinging down leg, wided.
Good comeback delivery from Mitchell Starc! This is bowled at over 144 clicks and swinging back in from middle, KL Rahul blocks it out.

FOUR! The pressure of a hat-trick ball? What's that? KL Rahul has hammered this one away. Pitched up outside off, trying to swing it back in, Rahul gets on the front foot and creams it through cover for a boundary.

Saved by the extra bounce! Sean Abbott bowls this from a bit wider of the crease and angles it on a length into the stumps. Shubman Gill leans forward to drive but is beaten by the swing and gets hit high on the pads. There is a huge shout for LBW and given! What is happening out there? Shubman Gill has reviewed it though. Nothing on UltraEdge again and Ball Tracking shows that the ball is going over the stumps, maybe it is Gill's day today.
Pitches it up on middle, pushed toward mid on.
FOUR! Uppish but in the gap! Good length, offering width and Shubman Gill throws his hands at it. Gill drives it uppishly but well wide of the man at point for a boundary.
And again! On a length and outside off, Gill lets it through to the keeper.
Length ball, pushed wider off the off stump, left alone by Shubman Gill.
Starts off with a lovely delivery in the channel around off, shaping it away. Shubman Gill looks to play at it but is well beaten.
KL Rahul walks out to bat now. Also, Sean Abbott comes into the attack.

OUT! LBW! Mitchell Starc is spitting fire out there and Suryakumar Yadav walks back for a golden duck. This is another pacy delivery, served on a perfect around off and nipping back in sharply. Yadav gets pushed on the back foot as he looks to drive but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is another huge appeal for LBW but this time, the umpire says no. Australia have reviewed it. There is nothing on UltraEdge but Ball Tracking comes up with three reds and the crowd inside the Wankhede is completely silenced.
Suryakumar Yadav comes out to the middle now.

OUT! LBW! Plumb in front and Virat Kohli doesn't even look back. Mitchell Starc goes full now, bowls it at a good pace and gets the ball to swing back in sharply from off stump. Virat Kohli falls over as he looks to flick and ends up playing all over a straight ball. The ball raps him on the pads and the finger is raised as soon as there is an appeal. Starc is rewarded for his top-class display of swing and India lose two early wickets.
Peach of a delivery! On a good length at 145.8 KPH, very close to the top of the off pole. Virat Kohli covers his line but the ball just goes straight on and zips past the outside edge.

Half an appeal for LBW but it is turned down. Good length around middle and swinging back in a long way. Virat Kohli shuffles across a bit and misses the flick, getting hit on the pads. Probably just swinging down leg.
Length ball around off at 140 clicks, a hint of shape into the right-hander. Virat Kohli looks to drive at it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

Sweet sound off the bat! Full and outside off at around 144 clicks, Shubman Gill reaches out and pings the cover drive off the middle of the bat. Marcus Stoinis gets a hand on it at covers and keeps it down to a single.
Bowled on a good length and pushed well outside off, Kohli shoulders arms at it.

FOUR! A real 'Hit me' ball from Marcus Stoinis and Virat Kohli is off the mark in style. A half-volley around off, Kohli drives it crisply and straight back past the bowler into the long off fence for a boundary.
Back of a length over middle, Kohli pushes it down toward mid on.
Good length outside off, Virat Kohli makes another leave.

Edged, but wide of the second slip! Length ball on off stump and straightening off the deck. Shubman Gill gets caught on the crease and gets an outside edge which just goes past the diving Steven Smith at second slip down to third man. A single is taken and Gill is living on the edge here.
This is very full on the off stump, Gill punches it straight to mid on.
Good length, on the fifth stump line and shaping back in late. Virat Kohli leaves it alone.
Shorter one on the body, Gill tucks it off his hips in front of square leg for a single.
Short of a length and around off, Shubman Gill chops it onto the ground as the ball goes nowhere.
FOUR! Adding insult to injury! This is very full around off, Shubman Gill just creams it through covers and picks up a boundary.

EDGED AND DROPPED! Mitchell Starc serves this one a perfect length around off at 144.9 clicks, swinging it back in. The ball straightens off the deck and Shubman Gill has to play at it. Gill gets an outside edge that goes low to the right of the keeper. Josh Inglis dives that side and gets a glove on it but spills it down. This could be a huge miss for Australia.
Loose shot from Shubman Gill! Shorter in length and pushed well outside the off stump. Gill doesn't move his feet and throws his hands at it, and is well beaten.
Virat Kohli walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! LBW! Marcus Stoinis strikes in his first over and Australia have the early wicket. This is bowled on a length around middle and simply skidding on. Ishan Kishan gets forward looking to tuck but gets pinged on the pads. There is a huge shout for LBW, and given! Ishan Kishan has a word with Shubman Gill and opts for the review. No spike on UltraEdge. Ball Tracking comes up with three reds and it is dead straight, the review is lost as well.
Just a fraction shorter around off, shaping in a touch, Ishan Kishan punches it in front of point and picks up a couple of runs.
This one is pitched up around off stump, Ishan Kishan defends it out with a straight bat.
Back of a length outside off, Shubman Gill stays back and taps it through cover-point for a single.
Pitches it up in the blockhole around off, swinging it away, Shubman Gill keeps it out on the full.
Starts off with a full and wide one outside off, Shubman Gill stands tall and strokes it on the up toward wide mid off.
Marcus Stoinis to share the attack.
Pacy delivery, on a length and in that channel around off, lovely shape on it as well. Ishan Kishan leaves it alone.
Length ball, swinging into the leg stump and bowled at over 145 clicks. Shubman Gill allows the ball to swing and tucks it away through mid-wicket for one. Gill too is off the mark.
Tries to angle this one into the pads, Ishan Kishan flicks it away wide of the fielder at fine leg to get off the mark with a single. India are underway!
Length ball around off, swinging away, Ishan Kishan keeps it out on the off side.
Full again, swinging it away from around middle, Ishan Kishan blocks it out.
Starts off with a fullish ball around off and gets it to shape away nicely from the left-hander. Ishan Kishan stays watchful and leaves it alone.
